Recognition and Presentation  Mayor Kendrick reported on the " Pride of La Verne Award Recipients.  He

Recipients -  and  the " Jim Scranton Award" to  recognize volunteers who  have  made

  outstanding contributions and performed exemplary service to the City

  plaque and their names are placed on perpetual plaques displayed in

 City Council Minutes, Tuesday, February 19, 2019, Page 3

The'` Jack Huntington  Award"  Mayor Kendrick reported on the origin of the" Jack Huntington Pride of
  La Verne Award". He stated that it was named after Jack Huntington who
  moved to  La Verne in 1970. Despite heavy professional obligations and time
  commitments to the U. S. Naval Reserve, Jack became actively involved in the
  community as a volunteer. He was active in various local organizations
  including the La Verne Jaycees, Little League and the Youth Basketball
  program. Jack also served as a City of La Verne Commissioner for more than
  15 years, completing two terms on the Parks& Recreation Commission as well
  as two terms on the Planning Commission. Jack Huntington was a citizen
  volunteer who exemplified the" Pride of La Verne" through selfless service to
  the community.

  Mayor Kendrick stated that this year the" Jack Huntington Pride of
  La Verne Award" is being presented to Jennifer Kesterson. He reported
  that Jennifer( with the help of her husband, Jim), has been the driving force
  and leadership of the Community Emergency Response Team( CERT)
  program  this past year. As a community coordinator and administrative officer,
  she  has logged over 1, 000 hours volunteer hours with La Verne CERT. Jen is
  often the face and voice of CERT, overseeing all e- mail communications,
  training enrollment, and event coordination. She also works closely with the
  LVFD CERT liaison and the Area D coordinator. Without Jen' s dedication and
  passion, as well as efforts towards teaching course units and creating program
  procedures, the La Verne CERT program would not be the success that it is
  today.

The " Jim Scranton Award"  Mayor Kendrick reported on the origin of the" Jim Scranton Award Pride of
  La Verne Award".  He stated that it was named after long time resident Jim
  Scranton who was a member of the Youth Sports Committee since its
  inception. In 1986, he formed the La Verne Lazers Soccer Club organization
  which provides youngsters an opportunity to play soccer at a highly
  competitive level. Jim also spent five years on the City Sports Park Committee,
  which resulted in the development of 35 acres of sports fields for the
  community.  He also participated in the City women' s soccer program as a
  coach. Jim is survived by his wife Susan and their children. The Youth Sports
  Committee recommended that a Pride of La Verne Youth Sports Volunteer
  Award be named in honor of Jim Scranton.

  Mayor Kendrick reported that this year the" Jim Scranton Pride of La Verne
  Award" is being presented to Natalie Ortiz. Natalie embodies all of the
  qualifications worthy of the Jim  Scranton Pride of La Verne Award,  and also

  lives her life in the same style that Jim Scranton did. She is always positive
  in the face of adversity, she never shows the exhaustion of an avid volunteer,
  she is always putting others before herself, and she never is looking awards
  or recognition.  Natalie has been an AYSO coach, referee and Board
  Member for 10+  years, Club Scouts Treasurer for 11 years, Boy Scouts

  Treasurer for 3 years, volunteering at Holy Name of Mary as a Scrip Manager
  and Annual Festival Finance Chair for 6 years, and a Damien High School
  Service Hours Coordinator for 2 years. On any given day, you will find her
  doing two or more of these activities. On top of this, she works in the Math
  Department at Loyola Marymount University, is  the wife to an equally
  awesome volunteer husband named Ray, who is a Fire Captain for the
  Glendale Fire Department, and she is a proud mother to 5 great kids( Anthony,
  Joey, Dominic, Nicolas, Talia), who, as you might suspect, volunteer as well.
   City Council Minutes, Tuesday, February 19, 2019, Page 4

  Recognition  of  Boy Scout  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, recognized and thanked Boy
  Troop 411  Scout Troop 411 for going above and beyond in helping military personnel
  during the recent Government shutdown. He stated that during the recent
  Government shutdown, the livelihood of Federal employees were impacted.
  One group in particular was the United States Coast Guard members and their
  families stationed in Topeka, Kansas. The Troop and their family members
  donated gift cards that were sent just in time for their next missed payroll.
  Scoutmaster Marsha Townsend represented the Boy Scout Troop 411.

7.  Conflict of Interest/ Carder/  Council Member Carder declared a conflict of interest because she is a
  Weed Abate Protest Hearing  member of the  Board of Directors for a homeowners' association that oversees
  property appearingon theweed abatementlist and left the room.

  City Manager Russi reported on the Weed Abatement Protest Hearing. He
  stated that on February 4, 2019, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 19-

  02, declaring that weeds, brush, rubbish, and refuse upon or in front of
  specified property in the City of La Verne, area are seasonal and recurrent

  public nuisance, and declaring its intention to provide for the abatement

  thereof. Notices to destroy weeds were mailed to property owners notifying

  them of a hazard or public nuisance upon their property and that same must
  be abated. That notice set Tuesday, February 19, 2019 at 6: 30 pm, as the date
  and time for protests to  be heard from affected property owners. The Annual
  Weed Abatement notice further required that owners of declared properties
  must maintain their parcels in a fire- safe condition throughout the year.

  Mayor Kendrick opened the public hearing and called for any protests and
  comments.  There was none.

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Hepburn, and carried by a vote of 4- 0
  Carder Abstained) to direct the Los Angeles County Agricultural
  Commissioner/ Director of Weights &  Measures to abate the nuisance by
  having weeds, rubbish, and refuse removed.

  Council Member Carder returned to the Council Chambers.

8.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Kendrick called for
  public comment.

  George May, La Verne Library Manager, reported on the La Verne Library
  events for the month of February. In addition, he reported that the Friends of
  the La Verne Library Committee are looking for new board members and
  officers. He stated that the current Board is comprised of long time members
  and officers and  many are seeking to retire. The Friends of La Verne are
  looking for infusion of new members and officers. He asked the City for
  assistance in looking for new members.

  City Manager Russi replied he would have the information posted on the City' s
  website.

  Gwen Carr, League of Women Voters, Mt Baldy 4bserver, introduced Barbara
  Nichols who will be replacing her as the Observer for La Verne and will
  attending the City Council meetings. Ms. Carr also reported the League of
  Women Voters Mt. Baldy is looking at expanding.

  Teri Muse, Public Sector Solutions Manager, Waste Management, extended
  an invitation to the Council and the public to attend the Waste Management -
  Azusa Transfer Station and Recycling Center Annual Open House on
  Tuesday, April 30, 2019 at 9: 30 am — 12: 00 pm/.
   City Council Minutes, Tuesday, February 19, 2019, Page 7

9.  Council Comments and  Council Member Hepburn spoke about the City of La Verne Community
  Meeting/ Conference Reports  Design Awards presentation and he stated it was nice to see the community
  recognized for their outstanding achievements in project development. He also
  reported on  the Sol Flower; Shota Sushi Restaurant Ribbon Cuttings. He
  stated  it was nice that La Verne now has 98 restaurants. He thanked
  everyone for coming.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis wished everyone a happy President' s Day.

  Council Member Rosales also spoke about the City of La Verne Community
  Design Awards presentation and it showed how wonderful La Verne is.  He
  thanked everyone for the positive comments and for coming.

  Council Member Carder also spoke about the City of La Verne Community
  Design Awards presentation and that it was nice to see Clive Houston- Brown
  formerly from the University of La Verne at the meeting.

  Mayor Kendrick reported on the Shota Sushi Ribbon Cutting and a Birthday
  Celebration for 95 year old WWII Veteran Frank Paglia. He stated that two
  other 1NW11 Veterans were also present and it was an amazing amount of
  history of the greatest generation of our Country that we owe our freedom to
  were sitting in that room. He reported that the Birthday celebration was
  sponsored by the America Veterans Assistance Group. He spoke about when

  the City of La Verne was named the top ten cities in America by Family Circle
  Magazine, which speaks volumes about La Verne and its residents. He
  thanked everyone for attending.
